description:
crate-jmap-sharing-server/src/lib.rs:226

    pub fn add_notification(&mut self, account_id: &str, notif_id: &str) {
        ...
        let mut guard = self.state.lock().unwrap();
        ...
    }

MockBackend is defined as:

    #[derive(Clone)]
    pub struct MockBackend {
        state: Arc<Mutex<HashMap<String, AccountState>>>,
    }

All mutation happens through self.state.lock() — i.e. interior mutability. The &mut self receiver is type-system noise that costs more than it buys:

1. Callers can't share a MockBackend between two paths that both need to mutate it. The natural shape — building an Arc<MockBackend>, registering handlers with one Arc::clone, and adding test fixtures through another Arc::clone — fails compile because Arc<MockBackend> only exposes &MockBackend.

2. The existing test at notification.rs:277-294 (set_mixed_create_and_destroy_enforces_destroy_only) sidesteps the issue by calling add_notification BEFORE wrapping in Arc. That works for the inline test but does not work for any test that needs to register a method handler and then add fixtures to the same backend instance — a common JMAP test pattern.

3. The constraint is meaningless from a soundness standpoint: Mutex<T> + Arc<Mutex<T>> is the canonical Rust pattern for &self-receiver-with-interior-mutation. The other in-tree methods on the same struct that mutate (account_exists, get_objects, etc.) all use &self correctly through self.state.lock(). The sole holdout is add_notification.

Idiomatic Rust: change &mut self to &self. The .lock().unwrap() body needs no change.

Sibling-scope: jmap-tasks-server/src/lib.rs:249 and jmap-calendars-server/src/lib.rs:303 both have add_notification(&mut self, ...) with the same pattern. Per the workspace 'Canonical Templates' rule, change canonical jmap-mail-server first if it has the same shape (it does not — mail-server has no add_notification because ShareNotification is a sharing-only type) — so this is either a sharing-family local convention to fix in three siblings, or a more general 'fixture-add methods on Arc<Mutex<>>-backed mocks' convention to align.

What goes wrong for callers when this stays as-is: any test that wants to register the mock through Arc and then add a fixture has to construct the Arc, take it apart with Arc::try_unwrap or .clone() into a Mutex-locked path, or restructure the test. The first two are awkward; the third is what every test currently does. A future contributor writes a multi-handler integration test, hits the &mut self barrier, and either reshapes the test or files this issue. Filing now saves the cycle.
notes: Changed MockBackend::add_notification from &mut self to &self. Updated the sole call site (notification.rs test) to drop the now-unnecessary 'let mut'. Interior mutation continues through Arc<Mutex<>>. Sibling shape in jmap-tasks-server and jmap-calendars-server tracked separately (sibling sweep).
title: MockBackend::add_notification takes &mut self despite interior mutability via Arc<Mutex<>>
